Now documents leaked to the Guardian have revealed its true scale . The Guardian’s Russia affairs correspondent, Pjotr Sauer , tells Helen Pidd what reporters have discovered. Two groups of hackers accessed Russia’s main statistics database last month and discovered a cache of 11m death certificates that revealed nearly 500,000 Russian losses in Ukraine since 2022. Among these were 1,000 – the equivalent of a whole regiment – who took their own lives. Continue reading...

articles.title: Why is scandal-plagued Jensen Huang back at Nvidia? – Stateside with Kai and Carter
articles.summary_snippet: Jensen Huang is apparently too big to fail – but what’s that mean for the rest of us? Just last week, Nvidia’s board chair told investors that the company had no intention of reinstating Huang as CEO. On Monday, they turned a full about-face. The board voted unanimously to reinstall Huang, triggering a nearly $1tn surge in the company’s stock market valuation. Donald Trump took credit, telling CNBC that he 'convinced them' to bring Huang back. But questions remain about Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and about whether Nvidia exploited loopholes to export chips to Chinese AI companies. Kai Wright talks with the Guardian US’s tech editor Blake Montgomery about the many twists and turns in the Huang scandal – and why Huang embodies the 'key man risk' that threatens our whole economy Continue reading...

articles.title: Europe’s big threat is not Trump and Putin redrawing the map. It’s our own learned helplessness | Natalie Tocci
articles.summary_snippet: The US and Russia lack the power to impose their will on the continent – the Shenzhen summit was no Yalta 2.0 The first ever trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin was rich in symbolism and empty of substance. Many Europeans, filled with anxiety about the Chinese, Russian and US presidents potentially colluding, saw chilling echoes of the Yalta conference in 1945, when Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt redrew the map of Europe. But those – particularly in eastern Europe – who are fretting about another historic betrayal should remember that when it comes to European security today, we are the ones who hold most of the cards. Far more meaningful last week than Shenzhen was a gathering in Berlin , held at exactly the same time. Continue reading...

Word spread quickly, and now Sharratt sees many members of the community, which numbers in the hundreds. He is what is called a “trusted messenger” – someone who understands a community and has earned their respect. Other trusted messengers can be neighbors, co-workers, customers, midwives, or people who work as long-distance drivers for the Amish. articles.title: The life, death and improbable rebirth of LA’s most beloved diner
articles.summary_snippet: For decades, it served pancakes, hash browns and steaks to hungry Angelenos. Then came closure, and a city mourned – but now the Original Pantry is back Sometimes, an old-school American diner is just a diner. And sometimes, like the Original Pantry in downtown Los Angeles, it feels like the heart and soul of a city, a bellwether of good times and bad. For decades it was famous for never closing. Located in a low-slung shotgun building on a busy corner, it fed politicians, movie stars, students, criminals and street bums around the clock, seven days a week. The doors had no locks, because the place had no need for them. The portions were huge, the prices dirt cheap, and many of the servers, in bow ties and white shirts, looked like extras from a Harold Lloyd two-reeler. Continue reading...

articles.summary_snippet: The Dutchman was under siege before pulling clear in the final lap Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton once again clashed on the track Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix with a remarkable, determined drive for Red Bull having done battle in a thrilling contest where the lead changed 35 times but the Dutchman remained absolutely indomitable, his skill and racecraft unmatched. His margin at the flag was just six-tenths of a second over the second -placed McLaren of Lando Norris, with his teammate Oscar Piastri finishing in third. World Champion Kimi Antonelli who was in the fight was fourth and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly in fifth. George Russell, who vied for almost the entire race for the lead, was unlucky in running over debris at the death causing him to lock up and drop to ninth. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
articles.summary_snippet: Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads. On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs. articles.title: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations
articles.summary_snippet: The effects of the continent’s coming polls will be felt far and wide – and could well turn into ‘key tests’ of the bloc’s resilience In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them. Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it. Continue reading...
